response.explanation: InvoiceController sits in the presentation layer. It imports InvoiceRepository from the persistence layer (line 2), receives it through its constructor (line 7), and its cancel() method calls repo.markCancelled(invoiceId) directly (line 15). The issue() path goes through the business layer (InvoiceService.issue, line 11), but the cancel path skips that layer and changes persisted invoice state with no business-layer logic in between. FF-S03 flags this because presentation should depend only on the layer directly below it (business), not jump to persistence. Here the jump means any cancellation rules (allowed state changes, authorization, side effects) can be bypassed, and the controller is tied to how storage works. No documentation, ADR or comment was provided that addresses this dependency. The fix is small and local: add a cancel operation to InvoiceService that wraps the repository call, then drop the repository import and injection from the controller. It ranks medium within the blocking tier because it is an unmediated write path, even though only one method is affected.
